liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Playin' In The Band** (2 reviews): Playin' flows into Shakedown a bit too quickly, before the band had loosened up in the jam; A first-set Playin' that transitions into Shakedown Street is highlighted as an exciting opening [18][24]
- **New Minglewood Blues** (2 reviews): Minglewood is hot, typical for the period; Reviewer considers this one of the better Minglewood versions they have heard [18][22]
- **China Cat Sunflower** (1 review): China Cat/Rider ending the first set is called one of the best from the Brent era [24]
- **Space** (1 review): Space sounds extremely out there, almost like instruments played backwards, with chaotic yet perfectly timed interplay [19]
- **Not Fade Away** (1 review): Not Fade Away is slow and funky [19]

## Setlist highlights

- **One More Set**: mythic rare: 2 archived performances [27]

## The recordings

- **gd1982-09-05.167589.shure.sm57.kelley.miller.clugston.flac1648** (recommended): audience recording; 17 songs; 128 min; rated 4/5 by 1 [1]
- **gd1982-09-05.nak300.sirmick.87210.sbeok.flac16**: source not stated; 17 songs; 123 min; rated 4.78/5 by 9 [3]
- **gd1982-09-05.142714.sbd.healy.streeter.dalton.miller.clugston.flac1648**: soundboard; 17 songs; 119 min; rated 5/5 by 2 [4]
- **gd1982-09-05.171785.nak700.menke.miller.clugston.flac1648**: audience recording; 16 songs; 126 min [7]
- **gd82-09-05.sbd-patched.warner.5490.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 16 songs; 119 min; rated 3.89/5 by 19 [9]. Said about its sound: Good soundboard sound, slightly wavy in places but not badly; Brent's piano is badly distorted during Shakedown; the mix is uneven, with Phil fading in and out; Things settle down by Minglewood, and the show gets into gear [15][26]

## Around the show

- Reviewer describes extreme heat, around 108 degrees, with no shade available [17]
- Fewer than 50 people sat near the stage on blankets at 9 AM, eating yogurt, bananas and granola [20]
- Up on the hill, about 50,000 people who had partied late for two nights were present [20]
- The Dead were added to the lineup only two weeks before, when Bill Graham took over [20]
- Reviewer disputes the 50-person claim; at 9:30 AM crowd was much smaller than the eventual ~150,000, but well over 50 [21]
- Several thousand people were present before the band started, though the large space made the crowd seem smaller [23]
- Garcia was quoted afterward calling it an average show, blaming the early hour and the heat [23]
- Some crowd audio between certain disc 2 tracks is missing [3]
- The China/Rider matches up with the versions from 8/7 and 8/10 [18]
- The 8-29 show is similarly funky and even slower, but no soundboard of it has surfaced [19]
- Set was short, yet longer than most or all other acts at the festival [21]
- The first set is more exciting and adventurous than many second sets [24]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1982-09-05.167589.shure.sm57.kelley.miller.clugston.flac1648**: taped by Ken Kelley; transferred by Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: Ken Kelley's Master Audience Cassettes; Shure SM-57 mics > JVC KD-2 w/Super ANRS (Maxell XLII-S90) [1]. Also: A Sony ECM 220T source from Rango Keshavan and Charlie Miller supplies a 26-second patch in Drums [1]
- **gd1982-09-05.nak300.sirmick.87210.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Unknown; transferred by SirMick; source: Nakamichi CM300 shotguns > Technics 686 > Maxell UD XL II [3]. Also: Nakamichi 300 source, sped-corrected because it ran slightly fast, with dropouts and pops repaired; First 33 seconds of disc 2 track 1 are patched from soundboard shnid 5490 [3]
- **gd1982-09-05.142714.sbd.healy.streeter.dalton.miller.clugston.flac1648**: taped by Frank Streeter and Tim Dalton and Dan Healy; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: flac16/48kHz ; Source Info: Dan Healy's Master Soundboard Cassettes (Sony TC-D5M/TDK MA-R90/Dolby B)> Frank Streeter's 1st generation 1/4 track Reels @ 3.75… [4]. Also: Sony ECM-220T source patches the opening of Playin', the end of I Know You Rider, and more [4]
- **gd1982-09-05.171785.nak700.menke.miller.clugston.flac1648**: taped by Bob Menke; transferred by Bob Menke, Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: Bob Menke's Master Audience Cassettes; Nakamichi 700 mics > Sony TC-D5M [7]. Also: Three-Sennheiser 421 source from Jim Vita and Charlie Miller supplies a 7-second patch in Drums [7]
- **gd82-09-05.sbd-patched.warner.5490.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [9]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Glen Helen Regional Park - September 5, 1982](https://www.dead.net/show/september-5-1982) [28]
- Poster by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Poster - The US Festival](https://www.dead.net/archives/1982/artwork/poster-us-festival) [29]
- Fan art by albumsthatshouldexist.blogspot.com: [US Festival '82, Glen Helen Regional Park, San Bernardino, CA, 9-5-1982 - Day 3, Part 1: The Grateful Dead](https://albumsthatshouldexist.blogspot.com/2024/12/us-festival-82-glen-helen-regional-park_94.html) [30]
- Poster by albumsthatshouldexist.blogspot.com: [US Festival '82, Glen Helen Regional Park, San Bernardino, CA, 9-5-1982 - Day 3, Part 4: Jackson Browne](https://albumsthatshouldexist.blogspot.com/2024/12/us-festival-82-glen-helen-regional-park_66.html) [31]

claims.text: Good soundboard sound, slightly wavy in places but not badly
Reviewer describes extreme heat, around 108 degrees, with no shade available
Playin' flows into Shakedown a bit too quickly, before the band had loosened up in the jam
Minglewood is hot, typical for the period
The China/Rider matches up with the versions from 8/7 and 8/10
Space sounds extremely out there, almost like instruments played backwards, with chaotic yet perfectly timed interplay
Not Fade Away is slow and funky
The 8-29 show is similarly funky and even slower, but no soundboard of it has surfaced
Fewer than 50 people sat near the stage on blankets at 9 AM, eating yogurt, bananas and granola
Up on the hill, about 50,000 people who had partied late for two nights were present
The Dead were added to the lineup only two weeks before, when Bill Graham took over
Reviewer disputes the 50-person claim; at 9:30 AM crowd was much smaller than the eventual ~150,000, but well over 50
Set was short, yet longer than most or all other acts at the festival
Reviewer considers this one of the better Minglewood versions they have heard
Several thousand people were present before the band started, though the large space made the crowd seem smaller
Garcia was quoted afterward calling it an average show, blaming the early hour and the heat
A first-set Playin' that transitions into Shakedown Street is highlighted as an exciting opening
China Cat/Rider ending the first set is called one of the best from the Brent era
The first set is more exciting and adventurous than many second sets
Brent's piano is badly distorted during Shakedown; the mix is uneven, with Phil fading in and out
Things settle down by Minglewood, and the show gets into gear
Source from Ken Kelley's master cassettes, a Shure SM57 recording, transferred by Charlie Miller
A Sony ECM 220T source from Rango Keshavan and Charlie Miller supplies a 26-second patch in Drums
Nakamichi 300 source, sped-corrected because it ran slightly fast, with dropouts and pops repaired
First 33 seconds of disc 2 track 1 are patched from soundboard shnid 5490
Some crowd audio between certain disc 2 tracks is missing
Soundboard DAT source provided by Tim Dalton, transferred by Charlie Miller
Sony ECM-220T source patches the opening of Playin', the end of I Know You Rider, and more
The second encore was performed at 9:30 AM at the Us Festival
Three-Sennheiser 421 source from Jim Vita and Charlie Miller supplies a 7-second patch in Drums
